mainTopic: Proof of conversion, conversion only in a בית דין, a father's believability about his children, and how a בית דין receives a גר
overview: The עמוד opens in the middle of a ברייתא about someone who says he is a גר. רבי יהודה reads ״בָּאָרֶץ״ to mean that only in ארץ ישראל must he bring proof. The חכמים say proof is needed everywhere. The גמרא works through the ברייתא's readings of the פסוקים, and רבי יוחנן rules like the חכמים. Next, רבי יהודה teaches that a conversion counts only in a בית דין. He tells a man who claimed he converted privately that he is believed about himself but not about his children. The גמרא asks how this fits with רבי יהודה's ״יַכִּיר״ rule, and רב נחמן בר יצחק and רבינא answer in two different ways. The הלכה follows רב נחמן בר יצחק. Finally, a ברייתא describes how a בית דין receives a new גר: it warns him about Jewish suffering, teaches him some מצוות with their punishments and rewards, and the passage continues on the next עמוד.

steps.title: The verse covers converts outside the Land too
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא learns from the word ״אִתְּךָ״ that a גר is accepted even outside ארץ ישראל.
steps.simpleTranslation: I would only know this rule applies in the Land. How do I know it applies outside the Land? The verse says 'with you', meaning: anywhere that he is with you.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא continues its reading of the פסוק about a גר. It shows that the rule is not limited to ארץ ישראל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says ״וְכִי יָגוּר אִתְּךָ גֵּר בְּאַרְצְכֶם״, so we might think the law of accepting a גר is limited to the Land. The extra word ״אִתְּךָ״ widens it to every place where a Jew lives.

keyTerms.meaning: I would only know (a limited case)

phrases.english: I have only in the Land;
phrases.notes: The ברייתא is working through ויקרא 19:33, which says ״בְּאַרְצְכֶם״, 'in your land'.

phrases.english: outside the Land, from where do we know?
The verse says: 'with you'
in any place that he is with you.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵין לִי אֶלָּא בָּאָרֶץ, בְּחוּץ לָאָרֶץ מִנַּיִן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא from the previous עמוד.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The rule of accepting a גר applies both in and outside ארץ ישראל, learned from ״אִתְּךָ״.

steps.title: Then why does the verse say 'in the Land'?
steps.stepSummary: If the rule applies everywhere, the ברייתא asks what the word ״בָּאָרֶץ״ is there to teach.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, why does the verse say 'in the Land'?
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא asks a question about the extra word. This sets up רבי יהודה's answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once ״אִתְּךָ״ has taught that the rule applies everywhere, the word ״בָּאָרֶץ״ looks unnecessary. A word in the תורה is assumed to be there for a reason, so it must teach something new.

keyTerms.meaning: What does the verse come to teach?

phrases.english: If so, what does the verse teach by saying 'in the Land'?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks what is left for the word ״בָּאָרֶץ״ to teach after step 1.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What the word ״בָּאָרֶץ״ teaches if the rule already applies everywhere.

steps.title: רבי יהודה: proof is needed only in the Land
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה says ״בָּאָרֶץ״ teaches that in ארץ ישראל a גר must bring proof, but outside it his word is accepted.
steps.simpleTranslation: In the Land he must bring proof. Outside the Land he does not need to bring proof. These are the words of רבי יהודה.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהודה answers the question by giving the word ״בָּאָרֶץ״ its own job: it teaches a difference in how much proof is required.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word ״אִתְּךָ״ teaches that a גר is accepted everywhere. The word ״בָּאָרֶץ״ teaches that only in ארץ ישראל must he prove his conversion. Outside the Land, his own claim is enough.

keyTerms.meaning: These are the words of רבי יהודה

phrases.english: In the Land, he needs to bring proof;

phrases.aramaic: בְּחוּץ לָאָרֶץ — אֵין צָרִיךְ לְהָבִיא רְאָיָה,
phrases.english: outside the Land, he does not need to bring proof;
these are the words of Rabbi Yehuda.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 2.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: ״בָּאָרֶץ״ teaches that proof is required only in ארץ ישראל.

steps.title: The חכמים: proof is needed everywhere
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים disagree with רבי יהודה and require proof both in and outside ארץ ישראל.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis say: whether in the Land or outside the Land, he must bring proof.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא ends with the opposing view of the חכמים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two sides argue only about whether a person who says he is a גר must bring proof outside the Land. The חכמים make no difference between places.
steps.whatToRemember: רבי יהודה: proof is needed only in ארץ ישראל. חכמים: proof is needed everywhere.

phrases.english: And the Rabbis say:
whether in the Land or outside the Land,
he needs to bring proof.

steps.triggerLanguage: וַחֲכָמִים אוֹמְרִים: בֵּין בָּאָרֶץ בֵּין בְּחוּצָה לָאָרֶץ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with רבי יהודה in step 3.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A person who says he is a גר must bring proof in every place.

steps.title: If he has witnesses, why is a verse needed?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the ברייתא needed a פסוק for a convert who came with witnesses, since witnesses are always believed.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he came with his witnesses, why do I need a verse?
steps.whatsHappening: Now the גמרא itself starts asking about the ברייתא. Its first question is about the case of a גר who came with witnesses.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier, the ברייתא used the פסוק for a גר who comes with his witnesses. But testimony of two witnesses is accepted everywhere in the תורה. So a special פסוק seems unnecessary.

keyTerms.meaning: Why do I need a verse?

phrases.english: He came with his witnesses;
why do I need a verse?

steps.triggerLanguage: בָּא הוּא וְעֵדָיו עִמּוֹ, קְרָא לְמָה לִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The ברייתא is finished, and the גמרא begins analyzing it.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's use of a פסוק for a גר who comes with witnesses.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Witnesses are always believed, so a פסוק teaching that they are believed adds nothing.

steps.title: רב ששת: the witnesses only heard about it
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת explains that the witnesses only say they heard he converted in a certain בית דין. Without the פסוק, we might not believe such testimony.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ששת said: The case is where they say, 'We heard that he converted in the court of so-and-so.' You might have thought they should not be believed, so the verse teaches us that they are.
steps.whatsHappening: רב ששת answers the question by narrowing the case. These witnesses did not see the conversion themselves.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally, testimony based only on hearsay might not be enough. The פסוק teaches that for a גר, witnesses who heard he converted in a known בית דין are believed.

keyTerms.meaning: It would enter your mind to say

phrases.english: Rav Sheshet said:
It is where they say: 'We heard that he converted
in the court of so-and-so.'
It might enter your mind to say
that they should not be believed;
so it teaches us otherwise.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב שֵׁשֶׁת: דְּאָמְרִי: שָׁמַעְנוּ שֶׁנִּתְגַּיֵּיר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 5.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Witnesses who only heard about the conversion should not be believed.
steps.terutzMaskana: The פסוק teaches that such witnesses are believed for a גר.

steps.title: Wasn't 'with you' already used?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the ברייתא's lesson from ״אִתְּךָ״ about outside the Land, and asks: wasn't that word already used for another lesson?
steps.simpleTranslation: 'In the Land': I would only know in the Land. How do I know outside the Land? The verse says 'with you', meaning anywhere he is with you. But didn't you already use that word for something else?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes again the part of the ברייתא from step 1, this time in order to challenge it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: One word in the פסוק usually cannot be used to teach two separate lessons. The earlier part of the ברייתא had already used ״אִתְּךָ״ for a different rule. So how can it now also teach about outside the Land?

keyTerms.meaning: But you already used it (for another lesson)

phrases.english: 'In the Land': I have only in the Land.
Outside the Land, from where do we know?
The verse says: 'with you,'
in any place that he is with you.
But didn't you already take it for something else?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the ברייתא's derivation in step 1 and asks a new question about it.
steps.kashyaTarget: Using ״אִתְּךָ״ to teach that the rule applies outside ארץ ישראל.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: That word was already used for a different lesson, so it should not be available for this one.

steps.title: Two different words: 'אִתְּךָ' and 'עִמָּךְ'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that one lesson comes from ״אִתְּךָ״ and the other from ״עִמָּךְ״, a similar word in another פסוק.
steps.simpleTranslation: One is learned from ״אִתְּךָ״ and one from ״עִמָּךְ״.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא resolves the question by pointing to two different words that both mean 'with you'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since there are two separate words in two פסוקים, each word can teach its own lesson. So no single word is used twice.

keyTerms.meaning: With you (a second word with the same meaning)

phrases.english: One is from 'with you' (itecha),
and one is from 'with you' (imach).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 7.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Only one word was available, and it was already used.
steps.terutzMaskana: Two separate words, ״אִתְּךָ״ and ״עִמָּךְ״, each teach their own lesson.

steps.title: How can the חכמים ignore 'in the Land'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the חכמים and asks how they can treat every place the same when the פסוק clearly says ״בָּאָרֶץ״.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis say: whether in the Land or outside the Land, he must bring proof. But it is written 'in the Land'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the view of the חכמים from step 4 in order to challenge it. The next step answers this.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה used the word ״בָּאָרֶץ״ to make a difference between ארץ ישראל and other places. The חכמים make no difference. So what do they do with that word in the פסוק?
steps.confusionAlert: Don't think the חכמים have been disproven. The next step answers this: they use ״בָּאָרֶץ״ for a different lesson.

phrases.english: And the Rabbis say:
whether in the Land or outside the Land,
he needs to bring proof.
But look, it is written 'in the Land'!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns to the view of the חכמים from step 4 and challenges it.
steps.kashyaTarget: The view of the חכמים that proof is needed everywhere.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The פסוק says ״בָּאָרֶץ״, which seems to make ארץ ישראל different from other places, and the חכמים ignore that.

steps.title: The word ״בָּאָרֶץ״ teaches that converts are accepted even in the Land
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים use ״בָּאָרֶץ״ to teach that we accept converts even in ארץ ישראל, even though we might suspect they only want its benefits.
steps.simpleTranslation: That word is needed for another lesson: even in ארץ ישראל we accept converts. You might have thought they only convert to enjoy the goodness of ארץ ישראל. Even now, when that goodness is gone, there are still לקט, שכחה, פאה and מעשר עני for them to gain. So the פסוק teaches us to accept them anyway.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from step 9. The חכמים say the word ״בָּאָרֶץ״ is not about proof at all. It teaches that converts are accepted even in ארץ ישראל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We might have suspected that people convert in ארץ ישראל only for the land's blessings, and even today for the gifts given to the poor. The פסוק says ״בָּאָרֶץ״ to tell us not to turn them away for that reason. Since the word is being used for this lesson, the חכמים do not need it to make a difference between the Land and outside it.

keyTerms.meaning: He needs it (this פסוק or word) for a different lesson
Goodness, the special blessings of the Land
Gifts for the poor from the field: fallen stalks, forgotten sheaves, and the corner of the field
The tithe given to the poor
It teaches us (so we do not make the mistake)

phrases.english: That word is needed by him for something else,
phrases.notes: "That word" means ״בָּאָרֶץ״ from step 9, and "him" means the חכמים.

phrases.english: that even in the Land we accept converts.
For it could enter your mind to say:
they are converting because of the goodness of the Land of Israel,
and even now, when there is no such goodness,

phrases.aramaic: אִיכָּא לֶקֶט שִׁכְחָה וּפֵאָה וּמַעְשַׂר עָנִי,
phrases.english: there are still gleanings, forgotten sheaves, the corner of the field, and the poor man's tithe,
phrases.notes: These are gifts for the poor. A convert could collect them, so we might suspect that is why he converts.

phrases.english: so the verse teaches us otherwise.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 9 against the חכמים
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redirects the פסוק to a different lesson
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Converts in ארץ ישראל should be suspected of converting for material benefit and turned away
steps.terutzMaskana: ״בָּאָרֶץ״ teaches that converts are accepted even in ארץ ישראל, so it is not about proof

steps.title: רבי יוחנן rules that every convert must bring proof
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן rules like the חכמים: whether in the Land or outside it, a convert must bring proof.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חייא בר אבא said in the name of רבי יוחנן: The הלכה is that both in ארץ ישראל and outside it, a convert must bring proof.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן gives the final ruling on the argument between רבי יהודה and the חכמים. He sides with the חכמים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה required proof only in ארץ ישראל. The חכמים required it everywhere. רבי יוחנן rules that proof is needed in every place.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אַבָּא אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: Rabbi Ḥiyya bar Abba said that Rabbi Yoḥanan said:

phrases.aramaic: הֲלָכָה, בֵּין בָּאָרֶץ בֵּין בְּחוּץ לָאָרֶץ
phrases.english: The halakha is: whether in the Land or outside the Land,
he needs to bring proof.
phrases.notes: "He" is someone who says he is a convert.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אַבָּא אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the practical ruling on the argument that was just defended
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Every convert, in the Land or outside it, must bring proof

steps.title: Isn't this ruling obvious?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why רבי יוחנן had to say this, since the הלכה always follows the majority against one opinion.
steps.simpleTranslation: That is obvious! When one Sage argues with many Sages, the הלכה follows the many.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי יוחנן's ruling as unnecessary. It is setting up the explanation that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה stands alone against the חכמים. By the usual rule we already follow the majority, so the ruling seems to add nothing new.

keyTerms.meaning: It is obvious, so why say it?
When one argues with many, the הלכה follows the many

phrases.english: This is obvious!
Between an individual and many, the halakha follows the many!
phrases.notes: The individual is רבי יהודה, and the many are the חכמים.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the need for רבי יוחנן's ruling
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The majority rule already decides like the חכמים, so the ruling seems unnecessary

steps.title: The ruling was needed because the פסוקים seem to support רבי יהודה
steps.stepSummary: Without רבי יוחנן's ruling, we might have followed רבי יהודה because the פסוקים seem to back him.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might have said that רבי יהודה's reason makes more sense, since the פסוקים support him. So רבי יוחנן teaches us that the הלכה is not like him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why רבי יוחנן's ruling was needed. רבי יהודה seemed to have a strong source.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says ״בָּאָרֶץ״, which seems to support רבי יהודה's difference between the Land and outside it. We might have thought this makes him an exception to the majority rule. רבי יוחנן tells us the majority rule still applies here.
steps.whatToRemember: The הלכה follows the חכמים: every convert must bring proof, in ארץ ישראל and outside it.

phrases.english: Lest you say:
Rabbi Yehuda's reason is more logical,
since the verses support him,
phrases.notes: He means the word ״בָּאָרֶץ״ from step 9.

phrases.english: so he teaches us that it is not so.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the פשיטא challenge
steps.terutzResolutionType: Shows a reasonable mistake that the ruling prevents
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Follow רבי יהודה because the פסוקים seem to support him
steps.terutzMaskana: The הלכה still follows the majority, the חכמים

steps.title: רבי יהודה: a conversion counts only in a בית דין
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא: from ״וּבֵין גֵּרוֹ״, said about judges, רבי יהודה learns that a conversion done in a בית דין is valid, but one done privately is not.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: ״And judge righteously between a man and his brother, and his convert.״ From here רבי יהודה said: One who converts in a בית דין is a convert. One who converts by himself is not a convert.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ברייתא. Here רבי יהודה shows from a פסוק that a conversion needs a בית דין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק speaks about judging, and it mentions the convert. רבי יהודה learns from this that conversion is a matter for judges, a בית דין. A private conversion does not count.

keyTerms.meaning: The Rabbis taught (this opens a ברייתא)

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
"And judge righteously between a man
and his brother, and his convert."
From here Rabbi Yehuda said:

phrases.aramaic: גֵּר שֶׁנִּתְגַּיֵּיר בְּבֵית דִּין — הֲרֵי זֶה גֵּר,
phrases.english: A convert who converted in a court is a convert;
if he converted by himself, he is not a convert.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic: how a conversion must be done
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A conversion is valid only in a בית דין, not in private

steps.title: The man who said he converted privately
steps.stepSummary: A man said he had converted privately. He had no witnesses but had children. רבי יהודה said he is believed about himself but not about his children.
steps.simpleTranslation: A man came before רבי יהודה and said: I converted by myself. רבי יהודה asked: Do you have witnesses? He said: No. Do you have children? He said: Yes. רבי יהודה said: You are believed to make yourself unfit, but you are not believed to make your children unfit.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a story that puts רבי יהודה's rule into practice. A man's own words hurt his own status but cannot hurt his children.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By רבי יהודה's rule, a private conversion does not count, so the man's claim makes him a non-Jew. A person is believed when he speaks against himself. Without witnesses, though, he cannot take away his children's status.

keyTerms.meaning: A story, an incident that happened

steps.confusionAlert: The man is not asking to become Jewish. He is saying his conversion never counted, so he is really not Jewish. That is why he is "making himself unfit."

phrases.aramaic: מַעֲשֶׂה בְּאֶחָד שֶׁבָּא לִפְנֵי רַבִּי יְהוּדָה,
phrases.english: There was an incident with one who came before Rabbi Yehuda,

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמַר לוֹ: נִתְגַּיַּירְתִּי בֵּינִי לְבֵין עַצְמִי.
phrases.english: and said to him: I converted by myself.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לוֹ רַבִּי יְהוּדָה: יֵשׁ לְךָ עֵדִים?
phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda said to him: Do you have witnesses?
He said to him: No.

phrases.aramaic: יֵשׁ לְךָ בָּנִים? אָמַר לוֹ: הֵן.
phrases.english: Do you have children? He said to him: Yes.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לוֹ: נֶאֱמָן אַתָּה לִפְסוֹל אֶת עַצְמְךָ,
phrases.english: He said to him: You are believed to make yourself unfit,

phrases.aramaic: וְאִי אַתָּה נֶאֱמָן לִפְסוֹל אֶת בָּנֶיךָ.
phrases.english: but you are not believed to make your children unfit.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַעֲשֶׂה בְּאֶחָד שֶׁבָּא לִפְנֵי רַבִּי יְהוּדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows רבי יהודה's rule from step 14 in a real case
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A person is believed about his own status but not about his children's status

steps.title: Does רבי יהודה really say a father is not believed about his children?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges step 15 with a ברייתא where רבי יהודה says a father is believed to make his son unfit.
steps.simpleTranslation: Did רבי יהודה really say a man is not believed about his children? A ברייתא teaches: ״יַכִּיר״ means the father can identify his son to others. From this, רבי יהודה said a man is believed to say 'This is my firstborn son.' In the same way, he is believed to say 'This son of mine is the son of a divorced woman' or 'the son of a חלוצה.' The חכמים say he is not believed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the ruling from step 15. It brings a ברייתא where רבי יהודה seems to say the opposite.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 15, רבי יהודה said the man is not believed about his children. But here רבי יהודה learns from ״יַכִּיר״ that a father IS believed about his son, even to make him unfit as a חלל. So why isn't the convert believed about his children?

keyTerms.meaning: 'He shall acknowledge.' The פסוק that gives a father the power to say who his firstborn is.
Firstborn son, who gets a double share of the inheritance
Son of a divorced woman. If his father is a כהן, he is a חלל, unfit for כהונה.
Son of a woman who had חליצה. With a כהן father, he is also unfit for כהונה.

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the two arguments. In this ברייתא it is רבי יהודה who says the father IS believed, and the חכמים who say he is not.

phrases.english: But did Rabbi Yehuda say
phrases.notes: The word in square brackets is part of the corrected wording, and it turns the line into a surprised question.

phrases.english: that about his children he is not believed?
But isn't it taught in a ברייתא:
'He shall acknowledge': he identifies him to others.
From here Rabbi Yehuda said:
A man is believed to say, 'This is my firstborn son,'
and just as he is believed to say, 'This is my firstborn son,'
so too he is believed to say:
'This son of mine is the son of a divorced woman,'
phrases.notes: He is talking about a כהן. If he says this, his son becomes unfit for כהונה.

phrases.english: or 'He is the son of a חלוצה.'
And the Rabbis say: He is not believed!

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמִי אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אַבָּנִים לָא מְהֵימַן? וְהָתַנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the ruling of step 15 using another statement of רבי יהודה.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יהודה's ruling that the private convert is not believed about his children
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי יהודה himself holds, based on ״יַכִּיר״, that a father is believed to make his son unfit. So he should be believed here too.

steps.title: רב נחמן בר יצחק: by your own words you are a גוי
steps.stepSummary: The man's own claim makes him a גוי, and a גוי cannot give testimony.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן בר יצחק said: This is what רבי יהודה told him: 'By your own words you are a גוי, and a גוי cannot testify.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן בר יצחק answers the question. He explains that the convert is different from a regular father.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ״יַכִּיר״ power only belongs to someone who can testify. This man admits he converted without a בית דין, and רבי יהודה holds that such a conversion doesn't work. So by his own words he is still a גוי, and a גוי's testimony counts for nothing, even about his own children.

keyTerms.meaning: A non-Jew cannot be a valid witness

phrases.english: Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak said:
This is what he said to him:
phrases.notes: רבי יהודה is talking to the man who said he converted privately.

phrases.english: According to your own words, you are a גוי,
and a גוי cannot testify.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק, הָכִי קָאָמַר לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 16.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the cases: the convert has no power to testify at all
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The convert is like any father who is believed through ״יַכִּיר״.
steps.terutzMaskana: A man who calls himself a גוי cannot testify, so ״יַכִּיר״ does not help him.

steps.title: רבינא: believed about his children, not his grandchildren
steps.stepSummary: רבינא answers differently: the man is believed about his children but not about his grandchildren.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא said: This is what רבי יהודה told him: 'Do you have children?' 'Yes.' 'Do you have grandchildren?' 'Yes.' He said to him: 'You are believed to make your children unfit, but not your grandchildren.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא gives a second, different answer to the same question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רבינא, the man IS believed about his children, just like any father under ״יַכִּיר״. What step 15 meant is that he is not believed about his grandchildren, because ״יַכִּיר״ only gives power over one's own sons.

keyTerms.meaning: To make unfit (to marry into regular families or to serve as a כהן)

steps.confusionAlert: For רבינא, the talk in step 15 really had a second question, about grandchildren. רבי יהודה's 'not believed' is about the grandchildren. The man is still believed about his own sons.

phrases.english: Ravina said: This is what he said to him:
'Do you have children?' 'Yes.'
'Do you have grandchildren?' 'Yes.'

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לוֹ: נֶאֱמָן אַתָּה לִפְסוֹל בָּנֶיךָ,
phrases.english: He said to him: 'You are believed to make your children unfit,'

phrases.aramaic: וְאִי אַתָּה נֶאֱמָן לִפְסוֹל בְּנֵי בָנֶיךָ.
phrases.english: 'but you are not believed to make your grandchildren unfit.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second answer to step 16, different from רב נחמן בר יצחק's.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי יהודה said the man is not believed about his sons, which clashes with ״יַכִּיר״.
steps.terutzMaskana: He is believed about his sons (״יַכִּיר״) but not about his grandchildren.

steps.title: A ברייתא supports רבינא: believed about a 'small' son, not a 'grown' son
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא quotes רבי יהודה: a man is believed about his minor son but not about his adult son.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ברייתא also teaches this: רבי יהודה says a man is believed about his minor son, but not about his adult son.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that seems to support רבינא. Its meaning will be explained in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא shows that for רבי יהודה, a father's believability has a limit. It does not reach every son in every situation. The next step explains that the limit really depends on whether the son already has children, which matches רבינא.

keyTerms.meaning: 'It is also taught so': a ברייתא that supports what was just said

phrases.english: It is also taught this way:
Rabbi Yehuda says:

phrases.aramaic: נֶאֱמָן אָדָם לוֹמַר עַל בְּנוֹ קָטָן,
phrases.english: A man is believed to speak about his minor son,
phrases.notes: He is saying the son is unfit.

phrases.english: but he is not believed about his adult son.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings support for רבינא's answer in step 18.
steps.raayaObject: רבינא's view that the father's believability stops at his son's children
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא quoting רבי יהודה about a minor son versus an adult son

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: 'minor' and 'adult' depend on having children
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן explains that 'adult' means a son who has children, and 'minor' means a son who has none, whatever his age.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חייא בר אבא said in the name of רבי יוחנן: 'Minor' does not mean an actual minor, and 'adult' does not mean an actual adult. A minor who has children counts as 'adult,' and an adult with no children counts as 'minor.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן explains the words of the ברייתא. This explanation is what makes it support רבינא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question is not the son's age. It is whether the son already has children. If he does, the father is not believed, because his words would also make the grandchildren unfit. That is exactly רבינא's point.
steps.whyThisMatters: This explanation links the ברייתא directly to רבינא's grandchildren rule. That is why the גמרא later says the ברייתא 'supports רבינא.'

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמַר רַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אַבָּא אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: And Rabbi Chiyya bar Abba said that Rabbi Yochanan said:
'Minor' does not mean an actual minor,
and 'adult' does not mean an actual adult.

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא, קָטָן וְיֵשׁ לוֹ בָּנִים — זֶהוּ גָּדוֹל.
phrases.english: Rather, a minor who has children is the 'adult.'

phrases.aramaic: גָּדוֹל וְאֵין לוֹ בָּנִים — זֶהוּ קָטָן.
phrases.english: An adult who has no children is the 'minor.'

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אַבָּא אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the words of the ברייתא in step 19.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: 'Minor' and 'adult' in the ברייתא depend on whether the son has children, not on his age.

steps.title: The הלכה follows רב נחמן בר יצחק
steps.stepSummary: The הלכה follows רב נחמן בר יצחק: the private convert is not believed at all, since by his own words he is a גוי.
steps.simpleTranslation: The הלכה follows רב נחמן בר יצחק.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rules between the two answers. It chooses רב נחמן בר יצחק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: So the man who says he converted privately cannot make even his own sons unfit. His own claim makes him a גוי, and a גוי cannot testify.

keyTerms.meaning: And the הלכה is like him

phrases.aramaic: וְהִלְכְתָא כְּווֹתֵיהּ דְּרַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק.
phrases.english: And the הלכה is in accordance with Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהִלְכְתָא כְּווֹתֵיהּ דְּרַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Decides between the answers of steps 17 and 18.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The private convert is not believed about his children, because by his own words he is a גוי and cannot testify.

steps.title: But the ברייתא supports רבינא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects: why rule against רבינא when a ברייתא supports him?
steps.simpleTranslation: But a ברייתא is taught in support of רבינא!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the ruling it just made.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Usually, an opinion backed by a ברייתא is stronger. Steps 19 and 20 seemed to back רבינא, so the הלכה should follow him.

keyTerms.meaning: But isn't it taught in a ברייתא

phrases.english: But isn't a ברייתא taught in support of Ravina!
phrases.notes: He means the ברייתא from steps 19 and 20.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the ruling of step 21.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ruling that the הלכה follows רב נחמן בר יצחק
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: An opinion supported by a ברייתא should win.

steps.title: That ברייתא is only about the ״יַכִּיר״ rule
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא speaks about a regular father using ״יַכִּיר״, not about a man who says he is a גוי.
steps.simpleTranslation: That ברייתא was said about the ״יַכִּיר״ rule.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. It shows the ברייתא does not really decide our case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא is about a regular Jewish father who is believed through ״יַכִּיר״, and how far that power reaches. It says nothing about a man whose own words make him a גוי. So the הלכה can still follow רב נחמן בר יצחק.
steps.whatToRemember: A father is believed to make his son unfit (״יַכִּיר״), but not his grandchildren. A man who says he converted privately is not believed even about his sons, since by his own words he is a גוי. The הלכה follows רב נחמן בר יצחק.

phrases.english: That one was said regarding the matter of 'he shall acknowledge.'
phrases.notes: It is about a regular father's power over his son, not about someone who calls himself a גוי.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 22.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the source: the ברייתא is about a different situation
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא proves רבינא's reading of our case.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא only covers ״יַכִּיר״ for a regular father, so the ruling for רב נחמן בר יצחק stands.

steps.title: The court first warns the convert about Jewish suffering
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that when a גר comes to convert today, the court asks why he wants to join a suffering people. If he answers that he knows and feels unworthy, they accept him immediately.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: When someone comes to convert nowadays, the court asks him: Why do you want to convert? Don't you know that the Jewish people today are in pain, pushed around, put down, and harassed, and that troubles keep coming upon them? If he says: I know, and I'm not even worthy, they accept him right away.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic by quoting a ברייתא about the first conversation a court has with someone who wants to convert.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The court does not try to sell Judaism. It describes the hardships of the Jewish people in exile to test whether the person really wants to join. If he accepts this humbly, there is no more delay, and the court begins the process right away.

keyTerms.meaning: The Rabbis taught; this opens a ברייתא
A convert, or someone coming to convert
At the present time, meaning during the exile

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the classic source for the practice of testing a potential גר by first pointing out how hard Jewish life can be.

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
A convert who comes to convert at the present time,
they say to him:
What did you see that made you come to convert?

phrases.aramaic: אִי אַתָּה יוֹדֵעַ שֶׁיִּשְׂרָאֵל בִּזְמַן הַזֶּה
phrases.english: Don't you know that the Jewish people at this time
are in pain, pushed around, cast down, and harassed,
and suffering comes upon them?

phrases.aramaic: אִם אוֹמֵר: יוֹדֵעַ אֲנִי, וְאֵינִי כְּדַאי
phrases.english: If he says: I know, and I am not worthy
phrases.notes: He means: I'm not even worthy to share in their troubles, but I still want to join.

phrases.english: they accept him immediately.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: גֵּר שֶׁבָּא לְהִתְגַּיֵּיר בִּזְמַן הַזֶּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic, the procedure for accepting a גר, after the conclusion about the private convert.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The court warns a potential גר about Jewish suffering. If he still wants to convert and speaks humbly, they accept him immediately.

steps.title: They teach him some מצוות, including gifts to the poor
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא continues: the court teaches the גר a sample of light and severe מצוות and stresses the sin of not giving לקט, שכחה, פאה, and מעשר עני.
steps.simpleTranslation: They tell him about some light מצוות and some severe ones, and they tell him about the sin of not giving the poor their gleanings, forgotten sheaves, the corner of the field, and the poor man's tithe.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא moves on to what the court teaches the person after accepting him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He is not taught the whole תורה at once, only "some" light and "some" severe מצוות. The gifts to the poor are named on purpose, because they are serious obligations that a newcomer might not expect.

keyTerms.meaning: They inform, they let him know
Gleanings, forgotten sheaves, and the corner of the field, all left for the poor
The tithe given to the poor

phrases.english: And they inform him
of some light מצוות
and some severe מצוות,
and they inform him of the sin of
gleanings, forgotten sheaves, the corner of the field, and the poor man's tithe.
phrases.notes: These are all gifts for the poor. The "sin" is failing to give them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same ברייתא with the next stage: teaching the accepted candidate.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The court teaches the גר a sample of light and severe מצוות and emphasizes the gifts to the poor.

steps.title: They warn him about the punishments for breaking מצוות
steps.stepSummary: The court tells the גר that as a non-Jew he was not punished for eating חלב or breaking שבת, but once he converts, these carry כרת and סקילה.
steps.simpleTranslation: They tell him about the punishments for the מצוות. They say: Know that before you reached this status, if you ate forbidden fat you were not punished with כרת, and if you broke שבת you were not punished with stoning. But now, if you eat forbidden fat you are punished with כרת, and if you break שבת you are punished with stoning.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא describes how the court makes clear to the גר the serious new responsibility he is taking on.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The court uses a before-and-after contrast. The same actions that carried no punishment for him as a non-Jew become very serious once he converts. This way he understands exactly what he is committing to.

keyTerms.meaning: To this status, meaning becoming a Jew
Spiritual cutting off, a heavenly punishment
Death by stoning, the court's punishment

phrases.english: And they inform him of the punishment for the מצוות.
They say to him: Know
that before you came to this status,
if you ate forbidden fat
you were not punished with karet.
If you desecrated Shabbos
you were not punished with stoning.
But now, if you eat forbidden fat
you are punished with karet;
if you desecrate Shabbos
you are punished with stoning.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא: after teaching the מצוות, the court explains the punishments for breaking them.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The court tells the גר that after conversion he becomes liable to כרת and סקילה for sins that did not carry these punishments before.

steps.title: They also tell him about the reward for מצוות
steps.stepSummary: Just as the court tells the גר about punishment, it also tells him about reward: עולם הבא is for the צדיקים. The ברייתא starts to explain that the Jewish people cannot receive their reward in this world, and the sentence continues on the next עמוד.
steps.simpleTranslation: Just as they tell him about the punishment for the מצוות, they also tell him about the reward for keeping them. They say: Know that עולם הבא is made only for the צדיקים, and the Jewish people at this time are not able to receive...
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא balances the warnings with encouragement by telling the גר about the reward for keeping מצוות. The sentence is cut off here and finishes on the next עמוד.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The court does not leave him only with fear. It teaches that the real reward is in עולם הבא, which is set aside for the צדיקים. The unfinished line begins to explain why the Jewish people's reward is not seen in this world.
steps.confusionAlert: The sentence stops in the middle at "לְקַבֵּל" (to receive). Don't try to finish the thought here. The ending comes on the next עמוד.

phrases.aramaic: וּכְשֵׁם שֶׁמּוֹדִיעִין אוֹתוֹ עׇנְשָׁן שֶׁל מִצְוֹת,
phrases.english: And just as they inform him of the punishment for the מצוות,
so too they inform him of the reward given for them.
They say to him: Know

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁהָעוֹלָם הַבָּא אֵינוֹ עָשׂוּי אֶלָּא לְצַדִּיקִים,
phrases.english: that the World to Come is made only for the righteous,
and the Jewish people at this time
are not able to receive

steps.triggerLanguage: וּכְשֵׁם שֶׁמּוֹדִיעִין אוֹתוֹ עׇנְשָׁן שֶׁל מִצְוֹת, כָּךְ מוֹדִיעִין אוֹתוֹ מַתַּן שְׂכָרָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Balances the punishments in step 26 with the reward for keeping מצוות.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The court also teaches the גר about reward: עולם הבא is reserved for the צדיקים.
